analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: FIMER DATA
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 38bps to 7,520 with a $4.3bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX -60bps at 27,740, Russell 2000 -72bps at 2,820, Dow -30bps at 52,231. Volume was 16.922bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.556bn.

October CPI surprised to the upside, with core +30bps against consensus of +20bps and strength broad across underlying components. The 10-year yield rose 10bps to 4.9896% and rate-sensitive pockets sold off.

Waller's overnight comments raised the possibility of larger policy moves if core inflation printed warm. The desk says this lets the market reopen the right tail on the policy path after the recent compression in hike risk.
The desk says the CPI print likely locked in a 25bps hike in December (market pricing is stated as '%110 probability') and one more hike in 1H 27.

NVDA fell about another 6% on an independent investigation, NYT reporting and a GOP-led House weighing a subpoena. The desk saw long supply in the name and very little defense given the uncertainty and the difficult macro and political backdrop.
AVGO (+3.8%) and AMD (+80bps) traded like primary beneficiaries of the NVDA news, while broader semis and AI names caught down with NVDA.
Excluding NVDA, market-wide volumes were light, with S&P 500 constituents tracking 15% below normal. The desk rated its floor activity a 5 on a 1-10 scale.
Asset managers finished moderate net sellers, driven by supply in large-cap tech. Hedge funds finished net sellers, with shorts exceeding longs, concentrated in tech and macro products.
Post-bell, CRWV rose 5% after Q3 revenue of $3.661b (guide $3.45b-$3.6b) and Q3 adjusted operating income of $379m (guide $200-$260m).
SPX realized less than the implied straddle on the day, with fixed-strike vols lower across the board. Skew was moderately bid but weaker than the aggressive offer of the prior day.
Index flow was quiet, mostly clients monetizing upside. The desk likes owning downside skew, with the street structurally short vol on the way down and long vol on the way up.

In single names, NVDA vol and skew are extremely elevated with little defense in cash or vol. The desk thinks selling vol via call-spread collars makes sense. The S&P implied move through end of week is 1.24%.
